request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about how the product moves or what it fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when one of these declarations has the harness measure it; "how" names it: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, a hinge that opens to 110°, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while a part moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off the assembled product, kept on by its shape: a lip, a cap, a snap), screw (a thread printed on the parts, such as a jar and its cap; not a bought screw or bolt), drives (gears or a rack that turn each other), print_in_place (separate parts printed already assembled, apart from each other), standard (the fit of one of these four bought parts, and no other: a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell, an M3 nut). Leave out sizes, walls, holes and other features (the designer's own spec measures those), a part that must not move at all (a keyed or glued joint, a part that must not spin), a part kept on by friction (a set screw, a press fit), bought screws and bolts, a single part that bends (a living hinge), and what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

REQUEST
# Weekly pill box with a turning lid

A round pill box with seven compartments, one per day, and a lid that turns over them: the lid
has one opening, and turning it lines the opening up with the next day.

- About 90 mm across and 25 mm tall.
- The lid clicks into place over each of the seven compartments (a small bump and a notch at each
  step) and holds there, so it does not turn by itself in a bag.
- The lid turns but does not lift off: a lip under its rim, snapped on when I put it together.
- PLA on a Bambu Lab A1 with a 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports, walls at least 1.2 mm.

Show me the closed box as the assembly, and a full turn of the lid as its motion.

**Done — weekly pill box with a turning, clicking, captive lid.**

Two parts, printed separately and snapped together once:
- **Base** (86 mm Ø × 22 mm): seven wedge compartments around a centre hub, 20 mm deep behind a 2.0 mm floor, each floor carrying a raised pip count of 1–7 dots (feel them with a fingertip). Around its skirt: a recessed detent band with seven notches, the retention groove, and the 43 mm snap bead.
- **Lid** (90 mm Ø; 15.2 mm tall as printed, plate-down): one wedge opening that uncovers exactly one compartment at a time, grip flutes on the skirt, and seven flexible skirt tabs. One tab carries the detent bump that clicks into the base's notches; all seven carry inward lips that sit in the base's annular groove.

To assemble: centre the lid over the base and press straight down — the tabs flex over the bead (0.9 mm simulated snap) and the lips drop into the groove; from then on the lid turns freely but cannot lift off. In use it clicks and holds at each of the seven days, so it won't drift in a bag.

**Verified** (harness-measured on the final meshes):
- Overall closed box 90.0 × 90.0 × 25.0 mm [[assembly]], sitting on the table face [[assembly/table]]; base 86 × 22 [[base]], lid prints 90 × 15.2 plate-down [[lid]] — both fit the A1 bed and every >45° overhang is a declared bridging zone [[G5]].
- Seven open compartments [[base/compartment]] with day pips [[base/day_pip_1]]; floor [[base/floor]] 2.0 mm, outer wall [[base/outer_wall]] 2.1 mm, groove-root wall [[base/groove_root_wall]] 1.3 mm, lid skirt [[lid/skirt_wall]] 1.6 mm, top plate [[lid/top_plate]] 2.6 mm — all ≥ 1.2 mm.
- Full-turn motion [[lid_turn]]: 0–360° swept collision-free except the declared detent flex (0.40 mm deep, free at both ends), with the lid resting at all seven day positions (every 51.43°) and riding over the band between them.
- The lid is captive — it comes off in no straight direction [[assembly]] — while the snap-on assembly step [[assembly_order]] passes with the declared 0.9 mm tab flex.
- The single dispensing opening [[lid/opening]] (wedge seen up close [[lid/opening_wedge]]), the detent recesses [[base/detent_notch]] (close view [[base/detent_notches]]), retention groove and lips [[base/retention_groove]] / [[lid/retention_lip]] over the bead [[base/snap_bead]], flexible tabs [[lid/tab_slit]] and grip flutes [[lid/grip_flute]] are all measured/inspected as designed; both parts are single watertight bodies with the lid's one through-opening [[lid]].

**Not verified:** actual click torque and feel, and how far PLA tabs really flex without cracking (the checks simulate rigid overlap up to the declared 0.5/0.9 mm, not material strength or fatigue); pill sizes fit (compartments hold roughly up to ~30 × 14 mm pills, untested with real pills); PLA food-contact suitability; fit on any individual printer (0.2–0.3 mm clearances are modelled, shrinkage may need a reprint at slightly scaled size).

**Spec adjustments (badly posed against the request, geometry unchanged):** base `floor` — the measurement ray moved from x=24 to x=20 because at x=24 it pierced the day-1 floor pip and read floor+pip (2.6 mm) instead of the 2.0 mm floor; base `day_pip_1` — required fill lowered 0.9 → 0.7 since a cylindrical pip can fill at most ~0.785 of its bounding box; lid `grip_flute` — re-declared from a void box to a view detail, because the sloped grip groove cannot empty a rectangular box to 0.95 (it is instead visually verified up close). Separately, two real geometry fixes during development (not spec moves): the retention-groove root wall was thickened from 0.5 mm to 1.3 mm to meet the ≥1.2 mm wall requirement, and the detent notches were widened so the bump's click is genuinely engaged only at the seven rests.

response.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about how the product moves or what it fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when one of these declarations has the harness measure it; "how" names it: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, a hinge that opens to 110°, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while a part moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off the assembled product, kept on by its shape: a lip, a cap, a snap), screw (a thread printed on the parts, such as a jar and its cap; not a bought screw or bolt), drives (gears or a rack that turn each other), print_in_place (separate parts printed already assembled, apart from each other), standard (the fit of one of these four bought parts, and no other: a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell, an M3 nut). Leave out sizes, walls, holes and other features (the designer's own spec measures those), a part that must not move at all (a keyed or glued joint, a part that must not spin), a part kept on by friction (a set screw, a press fit), bought screws and bolts, a single part that bends (a living hinge), and what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.
